notes_list.title: E/Z Configuration & Detailed Molecule Analysis
notes_list.basic_overview: E/Z nomenclature describes alkene geometry using Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) priority rules independently on each sp2 carbon.
notes_list.extra_info_content: CIP Priority Rules: 1. Higher atomic number gets higher priority. 2. If atomic numbers are the same, look at the next atoms along the chain (compare sets of atoms in decreasing atomic number). 3. Treat double/triple bonds as equivalent to bonded to 2/3 single atoms.
notes_list.examples: Detailed molecules discussed below covering atomic numbers, multi-atom chains, isotopes, and branching.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Strictly dependent on the absolute priority of groups on each alkene carbon, independent of carbon chain length or cis/trans ambiguity.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Split C=C into left and right carbons. 2. List atoms attached directly to each carbon. 3. Apply CIP atomic number rules to assign priorities (1 and 2). 4. Check spatial orientation: both high-priority groups on same side = Z, opposite sides = E.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: E/Z isomers are configurational stereoisomers (diastereomers) separated by a high rotational barrier due to π-bond overlap.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Crucial for identifying stereoisomeric products in elimination and addition reactions.
notes_list.common_traps: Don't judge priority by the size or length of the alkyl group; always look at the atomic number of the very first atom attached, and move down the chain only if there's a tie.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
must_revise: CIP rule tie-breaking in complex chains
Isotope priority assignment (e.g., D vs H)
